tasks.short: Write activities and observations in the lab notebook, copy instrument readings into the log, log sample movements and storage, and have the log reviewed and signed.

steps.what: Biological technician keeps detailed logs of work activities: in a paper notebook today, in electronic notebook templates after the change
Biological technician copies instrument readings into the log
Biological technician logs sample movements and storage locations: written by hand today, by scanning sample and location barcodes after the change
Biological technician has the log reviewed and signed by a colleague

tasks.design: Activities are logged in an electronic lab notebook ({DATA_PLATFORM}) with entry templates per protocol and automatic time stamps, instead of a paper notebook; the technician still writes each observation. Instrument readings flow in through instrument integration, and sample movements are logged by scanning barcodes in the laboratory system. Review and signing stay with a colleague, now by e-signature with an audit trail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Logs were handwritten and readings copied from instrument screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Laboratory systems barcode samples and log each change; notebooks take instrument data.
tasks.human_edge: Noting the odd smell or colour no instrument records.
tasks.altitude: The technician confirms entries instead of copying them.

reach.learn: Whether logs are complete and traceable.

evidence.claim: Thermo Fisher SampleManager LIMS barcodes samples, assigns tests and logs each change.
Official control labs must be ISO/IEC 17025 accredited, which requires validated software.

assumptions: Boundary: from lab work to the log signed; data analysis is outside.
Input contract: instruments connected; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.

Review and signing stay with a colleague. s1 keeps 80 because observations are a first record; the templates only fill standard fields and time stamps. s3 keeps 50 because each movement is still scanned and checked; only writing ids and locations goes.
Software is validated before paper logs stop.
research_questions: Do audit findings on records fall?

incremental.description: Biological technician keeps entry templates in step with protocols.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly free observations, so templates save little (s1 keeps 95), and few instruments connected (s2 keeps 70) (18.5); high: instrument-heavy work with many samples (37.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Program and run robotic liquid handlers and instruments, set up runs with sample lists, monitor runs, and transfer results to the laboratory system.

steps.what: Biological technician uses robotics and computer-interfaced equipment to run assays
Biological technician types sample lists into the instrument software
Biological technician monitors runs and handles errors
Biological technician transfers results from the instrument computer by spreadsheet

tasks.design: The laboratory system ({DATA_PLATFORM}) exports worklists with sample barcodes and positions to the robot and instrument software, and results flow back into the sample records, so sample lists are not typed and results are not moved by spreadsheet. Programming, running and monitoring the equipment stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sample lists were typed into each instrument and results moved by spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Laboratory systems exchange worklists and results with instruments.
tasks.still_hard: Each instrument vendor uses its own file format.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a pipetting head that is about to jam.

reach.learn: Whether results arrive sooner and without transfer errors.

evidence.claim: Thermo Fisher SampleManager LIMS barcodes samples and assigns tests.

assumptions: Boundary: from the assay request to results transferred; interpretation is outside.
Input contract: instruments with worklist import; fallback is typing.
Running and monitoring do not change.

incremental.description: Biological technician maintains worklist mappings per instrument.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older instruments without worklist import, so lists are still typed (s2 keeps 80) and results moved by spreadsheet (s4 keeps 70) (6.5); high: many plates a day on connected instruments (21.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare samples and reagents, run standardized tests, calculate results and compare them with limits, and record the results.

steps.what: Biological technician prepares samples and reagents
Biological technician conducts standardized microbiological or biochemical tests
Biological technician calculates results and compares them with limits in spreadsheets

tasks.design: Readings go from the instruments into the laboratory system ({DATA_PLATFORM}), where fixed formulas compute results and compare them with product limits, flagging deviations, so the technician does not calculate in spreadsheets or type results. Preparing samples and running tests stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were calculated in spreadsheets and typed into records.
tasks.enabler_now: Laboratory systems compute results and check limits by fixed rules.
tasks.still_hard: Plate counts and colour reads still need a person's eye.
tasks.altitude: The technician reviews flagged results instead of calculating.

evidence.claim: LabWare LIMS generates certificates of analysis with e-signatures and audit trails.
Official control labs must be ISO/IEC 17025 accredited, which requires validated software.

assumptions: Boundary: from the test request to results recorded; product release is outside.
Input contract: limits loaded per product; fallback is spreadsheets.
Testing does not change. s4 keeps 40 for manual reads such as plate counts, which the technician still enters, and for checking imported readings.
research_questions: Do calculation errors found at review fall?

incremental.description: Biological technician keeps product limits in the laboratory system current when specifications change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly manual reads, so results are still calculated (s3 keeps 60) and typed (s4 keeps 80) (7.5); high: instrument-read tests (17.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check reagent and consumable stock, look up items in supplier catalogues, fill the requisition, check it, and send it to purchasing.

steps.what: Lab staff scan each reagent and consumable barcode when they use it
Biological technician checks stock of reagents and consumables
Biological technician looks up laboratory equipment and supplies in supplier catalogues
Biological technician fills the requisition form
Biological technician checks the final requisition: items, quantities and suppliers against the reorder list, and the purchasing queue it goes to
Biological technician submits the checked requisition: by e-mail to purchasing today, by one submission in the purchasing system after the change

tasks.design: Reagent stock is held in the laboratory system's inventory ({DATA_PLATFORM}), reduced by barcode scans at use, with reorder points that list what to order. Items are picked from suppliers' punch-out catalogues in the purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}), which builds the requisition; once the technician has checked it, the technician submits it once to purchasing in the system. Lab staff scan items at use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock was checked by eye, items looked up and requisitions typed and mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Laboratory inventories and punch-out catalogues are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Special reagents are not in catalogues.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which lot of an antibody gave clean results.
tasks.altitude: The technician checks requisitions instead of typing them.

evidence.claim: Laboratory inventories with barcode scanning and punch-out catalogues are standard tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from stock low to the requisition sent; receiving deliveries and supplier contracts are outside.
Input contract: catalogues connected by purchasing; fallback is typing.
Purchasing handles system requisitions as they did e-mails. Lab staff scanning items at use is shown in s0 (share 1, other role).

approvals.approved_version: The requisition with its items, quantities and suppliers exactly as checked by the technician in s4, submitted once to the purchasing queue in the purchasing system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many special reagents outside the punch-out catalogues, so items are still looked up (s2 keeps 80) and typed into the requisition (s3 keeps 80) (27.2); high: mostly catalogue items (52.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The biological technician keeps running tests and instruments and reviewing results; handwritten logs, typed sample lists, spreadsheet calculations and typed orders shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the laboratory system and notebook
role.ambitious_version: A technician with more time at the bench.
